title: Unemployment benefits can extend the job search without equally improving jobs in concentrated labor markets
source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-24 using matched employer-employee LEHD data and quasi-random UI-duration assignment during the Great Recession
geography: United States; local labor markets, workers, employers, and Great Recession unemployment-insurance duration rules

observations.period: Great Recession UI-extension period; paper published April 2026

nonemployment_duration.value: UI extensions lengthened nonemployment by about one week

earnings.value: extensions produced economically meaningful but statistically nonsignificant earnings increases overall

concentration_gradient.value: the positive UI-earnings effect was significantly lower in more concentrated local labor markets

duration_gradient.value: local concentration did not change the UI effect on nonemployment duration

interpretation.value: improvements in job matches from extra search time were attenuated where employer market power was higher

observations.method: The author uses measurement error in state unemployment rates as quasi-random assignment of UI durations and estimates effects with matched employer-employee data from the Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program.
observations.uncertainty: This is a Census CES working paper and not a Census Bureau endorsement. The abstract reports the average and concentration interaction but does not establish the exact household budget, job-quality, bargaining, health, or long-run mobility consequences for each worker.
observations.subgroup: Workers exposed to different local labor-market concentration levels during the Great Recession; effects may differ by industry, occupation, age, race, gender, prior earnings, family resources, and benefit eligibility.
observations.counterinterpretation: Concentration may proxy for industry mix, place, worker composition, or other labor-market conditions rather than employer power alone. Longer nonemployment can reflect better search, weaker demand, benefit rules, health, care, or selection; earnings are not the same as job quality or household security.

related_sources.claim: The official paper provides the LEHD design, UI-duration assignment, concentration measures, earnings results, and match-quality interpretation.

boundary: This record adds a safety-net-to-search-to-job-match pathway conditioned by local employer concentration. It does not establish a universal employer-monopsony effect, household welfare, job quality, bargaining power, or later political or cultural action.
